lawyer: Mr. Goutam Kumar Roy, Advocate, For the Petitioners
parties:
Sukchand Kirtonia and another
Vs.
Rajubala Pramanik and others
full_judgment: 3. Defendant No. I contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit has no cause of action; barred by limitation and defect of parties. Further case of the defence are that, she is the wife of late Sridas Pramanik and the suit property belonged to her husband and after the death of her husband she inherited the property as widow for life time. It is also stated that the plaintiff did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property since the defendant No. 1 is still alive. The defendant No. 1 has been possessing the same on payment of rent to the government and she purchased 27 sataks of land under S.A. khatian No. 370 by a registered deed dated 16.04.1988 from some co-sharers and she is 8 annas share holder in the suit property by purchase and 8 annas by inheritance. The alleged cause of action for filing the suit is false and fabricated. The defendant No. 1 did not utter a single word regarding transfer of the property on 18.04.2004 as stated in the plaint. The plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property and has not yet inherited the property in any way and as such, the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff has no prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in their favour.
